solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run into trap that's found in meadow

indicators.note: the word for run is put into the word for trap, splitting it after its fourth letter

parts.note: to corner someone is to trap them
to run, as water does, is to flow

explanation.surface: Someone sets a trap in a meadow and a rabbit runs straight into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' and 'trap' read as a hunting scene; neither is the definition, which is the whole phrase about the meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild blue flower that grows in fields and meadows, so it is something found there.

clue.text: Took fifty per cent cut, adding 'Yes, that's satisfactory'

indicators.note: the word for yes is added on after the halved word
half of the word took is cut away, leaving only its latter two letters

parts.note: aye, often spelt ay, is an old or dialect word for yes, as in a vote

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a half-price cut and pronounces themselves content with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty per cent cut' halves TOOK, keeping OK; 'adding' attaches AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is the informal word meaning acceptable, all right, just about good enough.

clue.text: Thought 'Turn on' and it's turned on

indicators.note: turn tells us to flip the following little word around end to end
turned says the word it just before should be flipped round end to end

explanation.surface: Someone considers switching something on, and finds it already switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' makes NO from ON; 'turned' makes TI from IT; the final 'on' stays as written: NO + TI + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or belief held in the mind, a synonym for a thought.

clue.text: Kid number three: a hybrid

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross-bred mixture, so these letters are blended into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A child is introduced as the third in line, and a crossbreed besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' rearranges L (fifty) with THREE and A. 'Kid' looks like a child; here it is kidskin, the soft goatskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is soft leather made from young goatskin, used for gloves, so it is a type of the material.

clue.text: Document penned a long time ago

definitions.meaning: a formal legal order issued by a court is a kind of document
the archaic past participle of write, as in Holy ..., meaning written in olden days

explanation.definitionFit: A legal summons is a formal document; the same form is also an old past participle of the verb to write.

clue.text: Grass getting convict back in captivity is wined and dined

indicators.note: the reversed word for convict is held captive inside the word for grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places

indicators.note: back says the word for convict is read from its end to its start

parts.note: lag is British slang for a convict, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: An informer who gets a prisoner returned to jail is treated to a lavish dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a police informer, as in British slang, but it is the plant; a lag is an old convict.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain them lavishly with food and drink, so to be feasted and treated.

clue.text: Wonderful definition of master criminal?

definitions.meaning: an informal, rather dated exclamation of approval meaning marvellous
a top-notch swindler would be a super cheat, a superior deceiver

explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming phrase is slang for excellent, and read literally it describes an outstanding con artist.

clue.text: For which we eat an apple a day and toast

definitions.text: For which we eat an apple a day
definitions.meaning: the proverb says an apple a day keeps the doctor away, so the fruit is eaten to stay well
a drinking toast wishing those present well, said as glasses are raised

explanation.definitionFit: Staying well is the purpose of the proverbial daily apple, and the phrase is also a common toast when drinking.

clue.text: Game could start off badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the remaining letters are put together wrongly, in a muddled order
start off means the first letter of could is removed

explanation.surface: A sporting contest might begin poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' drops C from COULD, leaving OULD; 'badly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple board game played with dice and counters, the British version of the Indian game pachisi.

clue.text: Too old for love, or just not bothered?

definitions.meaning: read literally, beyond the age of caring for a sweetheart
the idiom for having stopped worrying about something at all

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means no longer worried about something; read literally it suggests being past the age of tender affection.

clue.text: Add a very soft conclusion

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: An instruction to finish something quietly, perhaps a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach or tack on at the end, a synonym of add.

clue.text: Key change singer withdraws, being apprehensive

parts.note: C is a musical key

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of singer

explanation.surface: A vocalist backs out of a performance, worried about a modulation in the song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key change' looks like a musical modulation, but the two words do separate jobs: a single letter, then an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to shrink back or recoil in fear or embarrassment, flinching away nervously.

clue.text: Latin lover

parts.note: not a romantic Mediterranean charmer but someone who loves the Latin language and its literature

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a smouldering suitor; read literally it is a devotee of Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of ancient Greek and Roman languages is literally a person devoted to Latin.

clue.text: So cheese is in tiny wrapping, Highness

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the wrapping of a word is its outside letters, here the first and last of tiny

explanation.surface: A snack is presented in a little package and offered to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' takes TY, the outside letters of TINY. 'Highness' looks like a royal title, but it means being high, that is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being high, in the sense of intoxicated, is the opposite of sober, so drunkenness.

clue.text: Rescues a number trapped by rising waters

indicators.note: the number is caught inside the reversed word for waters
in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: seas are bodies of water
V is the Roman numeral five, a number

explanation.surface: A lifeboat crew pulls several people out of a rising flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SEAS into SAES; 'trapped by' puts V inside. 'rising waters' reads as a flood but splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone is to rescue them from danger, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Northerner's rendering of 'Ogre, meet thine end'

indicators.note: a rendering is a version, so the letters of ogre are given in a new form

parts.note: to meet one's end is to die

explanation.surface: A local from northern England delivers a line from a fairy tale in his own dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Tyneside, around Newcastle in north-east England; 'rendering of' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Tyneside in north-east England is a person from the North of the country.

clue.text: He hands over soldier. Clergyman accompanies back

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for a clergyman is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A soldier surrenders, and a priest walks beside him back to camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REV into VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hands things over is one who donates or bestows them.

clue.text: Mad to free hand caught

indicators.note: the word for hand is caught inside the word for to free

parts.note: to rid someone of something is to free them of it
a deck hand is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: Someone is furious that a hand they caught was let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' looks like a body part; it is a sailor, an able seaman. 'caught' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means wildly fanatical or raving, synonymous with mad or crazed.

clue.text: Furthermore, there's a capital orchestra

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, based in the capital

explanation.surface: An extra point: the city has its own orchestra too.
explanation.definitionFit: Also introduces an additional point, the same role as besides or in addition.

clue.text: Beautiful stone work on interior of wall

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music

indicators.note: the interior of a word is its letters without the first and last

explanation.surface: A lovely gem has been set into the inside of a wall as decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior of' takes AL, the inside letters of WALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent gemstone prized for its shifting colours, so a beautiful stone.

clue.text: Hard to shorten or cut

indicators.note: shortening the word for hard means taking its last letter off

parts.note: severe means hard, harsh
the E taken off is the final letter of severe, which is what shortening the word removes

explanation.surface: A choice between trimming something or chopping it off entirely is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shorten' docks the final letter. 'Hard' reads as the start of 'hard to shorten', a difficulty, but it is a synonym in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut off or cut through, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Launches parodies

definitions.meaning: sends something up into the air, as a rocket is launched
mocks by imitation, in British idiom

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb literally means propels upward, and in British idiom also means mocks by satirical imitation.

clue.text: He doesn't like people about, having clues to unravel

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: unravelling the clues means teasing their letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who dislikes company has a puzzle to work out on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does double duty, ending the definition and giving RE; 'to unravel' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is a hermit who shuns society, so someone who avoids company.

clue.text: Checks contributions unpaid going in

indicators.note: the word for unpaid goes inside the word for contributions

parts.note: subs are subscriptions, regular payments made to a club
a debt that is due is still owed, not yet paid

explanation.surface: Someone checks which membership payments are still outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' looks like inspects; here it is restrains. 'going in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue is to restrain or hold back, as to check something is to curb it.

clue.text: Second delivery?

parts.note: not a second post round but being born a second time, a spiritual renewal

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a postal round; delivery here is childbirth, so the birth happens again.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal or revival is figuratively being born again, so a second birth.

clue.text: Is concealing myriad aspirations

indicators.note: the word is hides the word for myriad inside itself

parts.note: a great deal is a myriad, a very large amount

explanation.surface: A statement that something hides countless hopes and dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'myriad' stands for 'a great deal'; 'concealing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection one aims for, so goals or hopes.

clue.text: Wound up drunk after last of cognac

indicators.note: the word for drunk comes after the letter from cognac
the last of a word is its final letter, here from cognac

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone ended up tipsy once the brandy was finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' looks like ended up; it is the past of wind, as a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Coiled means twisted into a spiral, so wound round and round like a spring.

clue.text: He barks loud reply to 'Do you take…?'

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a wedding vow answers the question with I do

explanation.surface: A dog barks back noisily when asked a question at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional stock name for a pet dog, the creature that barks.

clue.text: Seen on US map, it takes one right back

indicators.note: back tells us the run of letters taken from one right is read in reverse
takes signals that the letters are lifted straight out of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller studying a US map finds it takes him right back to where he started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' lifts ONER from 'one right' and 'back' reverses it. RENO is a city in Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno is a city in Nevada, so a place marked on a map of the United States.

clue.text: Plus it got built by arranged date, as specified

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two rearranged parts sit side by side
built up from the letters, so plus it is reassembled in a new order
arranged means the letters of date are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A building was finished by the agreed date, just as the contract required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got built' rearranges PLUS IT to STIPUL; 'arranged' turns DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to lay down as a condition, so stipulated means specified in terms.

clue.text: A lot to be said for — a lot

indicators.note: to be said signals the word for a lot is spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: a sight means a great deal, as in a sight better

explanation.surface: Something has a great deal in its favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' first means a great deal, as in 'a sight better'; the second 'a lot' is a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A lot is a plot of land, especially one for building, so a location or plot.

clue.text: Calling for a declaration

definitions.meaning: a vocation or occupation, such as law or medicine
a public avowal, as in a ... of faith

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an occupation or vocation and an open avowal of belief.
